name: Misata Studio
tagline: Browser based studio that generates design output from a parametric, rule driven engine instead of hand drawing it.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The scary part of a generator like this is usually not the math. Seeded pseudo randomness, noise fields, Poisson disk sampling, constraint solving and perceptually even color in OKLCH are all textbook primitives an agent can assemble in an afternoon, and the output will look like a generator from 2014 unless someone tunes it. What you cannot one-shot is the parameter ranges and presets that make every roll of the dice look deliberate, which is taste encoded as hundreds of small decisions. So you get a working engine in a weekend and spend the following month discovering that 95 percent of your seeds are ugly. Verdict is kinda: the machine is easy, the curation is the product.
coreLoopDIY: Builds a local parametric generator with a seed, a parameter panel, a live canvas preview and SVG plus PNG export, so you can roll, tweak and keep the outputs you like.
requirements: Comfort with seeded PRNG, noise functions and basic geometry
Color handling in OKLCH or similar, not raw RGB guessing
Patience to hand-tune parameter ranges until random stops looking random
whatYouLose: Curated presets that make the average output presentable instead of a math demo
Export plumbing that actually opens cleanly in Figma, Illustrator or a print workflow
Whatever clever constraints keep the engine from producing visual mush
Updates and new generators you did not have to design yourself
Any clarity about commercial licensing of what you produce, which you now own entirely and also have to think about
moatNotes: The engine is replicable. The parameter space someone already pruned for you is the thing you are actually renting.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because people buying a generator are buying the absence of fiddling. The paid version hands you something usable on the third click; the DIY version hands you a slider panel and a long evening. If you generate assets occasionally, paying is obviously correct. If you need a specific repeatable look for one project, or you want the engine wired into a build script to produce a thousand variants, the local build wins outright and costs nothing per run.
notes: Math engines sound like moats and almost never are. The real work is deciding which of the infinite outputs are allowed to exist.
prompt:
Build a local-first generative design studio as a single-page web app. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Vite + TypeScript + React, plain CSS modules, zustand for state. Rendering to SVG via direct DOM, with an offscreen canvas path only for PNG rasterizing. No design system libraries.

Core model:
- A "composition" is defined entirely by a seed string plus a flat parameter object. Same seed plus same params must always render pixel-identical output.
- Implement a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 or sfc32), seeded from a hashed string. Never call Math.random anywhere.
- Implement these primitives in src/engine: value noise and 2D simplex-style noise, Poisson disk sampling, a weighted-choice helper, and a golden-ratio sequence for spacing.
- Implement at least three generators that share one interface: (a) layered noise contour fields, (b) recursive subdivision of a rectangle into a grid of shapes, (c) flow field of stroked paths. Each exports its own parameter schema with min, max, step and default.

Color: convert through OKLCH, not HSL. Build palettes from a base hue plus rules (analogous, split complement, mono) and clamp lightness so output never turns to mud. Ship 8 hand-picked palettes as presets.

UI:
- Left: parameter panel generated automatically from the active generator's schema.
- Center: live preview, debounced re-render, show the current seed.
- Right: a "roll" button, a pinboard of saved outputs stored in localStorage (seed + params only, re-rendered on load), and export buttons.
- Keyboard: space to roll a new seed, cmd+z to undo the last parameter change.

Export: SVG with grouped layers and no inline junk, PNG at 1x/2x/4x, and a JSON file containing seed plus params. Importing that JSON must restore the exact composition.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, cloud sync, sharing links, animation export, a plugin system, any AI model calls.

Include a presets.ts with at least 12 curated parameter sets per generator, tuned so a random preset looks intentional. Treat this file as the real product.

If you need any secret at any point, read it from .env and document it in README. You should not need one.

Finish with: npm run dev working from a clean clone, and a README explaining the engine interface so new generators can be added in one file.
